why: Judge 2 was right; I confirm the steps. (1) In v4 any member takes a write and cells merge by last-writer-wins on Lamport stamps (SPACE section 2: R `lww`; O `lamp`, 'no total order per partition'). (2) So two members that each take a write to another field of one row apply the two in opposite orders: one copy shows {x} then {x, y}, the other {y} then {x, y}, and no one log has both as folds of its prefixes. (3) P-01 asks for per-partition order, which REQUIREMENTS reads as total, and tests that every replica equals the fold of the committed log; v4 has no such log, and getting one needs another row's R and O options. Judge 1's verdict here was the default text about E-22's Raft prototype, which is not v4's mechanism.

Judge 2 was right; I confirm the steps. (1) P-02 asks that all copies agree on which rows exist at each log position, and that a row expires within one tick plus `skew.max` of its ttl. (2) v4 has no time rule (T is empty in SPACE 4.1), no log position per partition (O `lamp`), no `ttl` or `max` in its API, and no one writer to judge a condition (SPACE section 5: `lww` forbids conditions). (3) So an expiry is each member's own guess by its own clock: a remove written on one member and a `touch` on another merge by stamp, not by time, so a touched row can go early or copies can differ. The cure is one writer and writer time, which are other rows' R and T options, so the row fails as it stands. Judge 1 named the same gap ('no test on it') and called it open.

Judge 2 was right; I confirm the steps. (1) Any v4 member takes a publish, each origin keeps its own log, and records merge by Lamport stamp (R `lww`, O `lamp`: no total order per partition). (2) Two publishes to one subject through two members are applied in arrival order on each copy, so two subscribers on two members can get them in opposite orders. (3) P-06 asks for order per subject, which REQUIREMENTS reads as total per partition; both judges already fail V4 on P-07 for this same lack of one order. Judge 1's verdict here was the default text about E-22's Raft prototype.

Judge 2 was right; I confirm the steps. (1) P-13 has two halves: a lapsed session's rows go on every copy within its lease plus one tick, and a live session's rows never go; whether a session has lapsed is a condition on its renewals, by one clock. (2) v4 has no time rule (T is empty in SPACE 4.1) and no one writer to judge a condition (R `lww`; DESIGN-V5 section 9 measured two claims judged on local state that both committed). (3) So a member that has not seen a renewal removes a live session's rows, and the remove stands if its stamp is higher; or renewals win, and a late one brings a removed row back (STATUS's open bug: a write from an evicted member beats a newer remove). One half breaks either way, and the cure is another row's R and T options. Judge 1 named the same gap and called it open.

Judge 2 was right; I confirm the steps. (1) P-16 asks to keep every fact and to rebuild a projection equal to the live one byte for byte. (2) v4 keeps one log per origin and compacts it: an entry that is not its cell's winner is dropped ('loser history vanishes, by construction', kernel/log.ts), and v4 has no `history: 'all'`. (3) So an overwritten fact is gone, and there is no one order to replay what is left (O `lamp`); keeping every fact in one order needs another row's R and O options. Judge 1's verdict here was the default text about E-22's Raft prototype and data's contract.

Judge 2 was right; I confirm the steps. (1) P-20's MUST rests on P-16's rebuild from `history: 'all'` and on old records passing through upcasters. (2) v4 keeps no full history (compaction drops every entry that is not its cell's winner, kernel/log.ts) and has no shape version or upcaster; with no log position per partition (O `lamp`) two members can also fold one record under two versions during a roll. (3) So there is nothing to rebuild from, and the MUST fails with P-16. Judge 1's verdict here was the default text about E-22's Raft prototype.

Judge 2 was right; I confirm the steps. (1) P-10 asks that a write with an older token than one a writer has seen is refused, and TEST-13's checker reads that per log and per lock (E-22's `fence-log`). (2) On JetStream the judge is fero's client, which compares the token in the last message of one subject, one row; the only wider condition is the whole stream's last sequence, which any other write breaks (E-44, gaps 4 and 6; both judges fail BUY on P-14 for this same limit). (3) So after the new holder writes row A under token 61, the paused holder's write to row B under token 60 passes its check and is stored after the newer token in the same log. E-44 lists 'fencing that every write passes through' as needing a kernel fero owns, so the cure is another row's writer. What E-44 measured still holds: 60 acquires, never two holders, and an older token refused on the same row.

But the SHOULD also says the migration is paced so P-01's p99 holds during a roll, and its test is a migration under load: no run timed a write's p99 beside a migration (the simulation has no real clock), and P-01's p99 is itself open; judge 2 says the same ('not timed') and holds P-08 and P-22 open for a bar that was never timed.

closes: A migration across three versions on example 43 under real load, with P-01's write p99 pinned during a roll (after P-01's own pin).
